Subject: Request: traffic hedge + version pin authorization for Tressel Health POC

Team —

Quick ask: Tressel (POC for their patient intake assistant) is contractually asking us to guarantee a 99.95% availability and a p95 latency target of <400ms for the public endpoint during the 2-week pilot. Given this is a POC traffic pattern, I want to propose a conservative rollout policy that we can ask Legal/Finance to accept as an SLA mitigation:

Plan (high level) —
- Start: 12% canary traffic (A/B style) to new model variant (v2-quant)
- Safety net: automatic fallback to v1 on sustained errors, and forced version pin for 48 hours if we detect regressions
- Telemetry gating: autorevert if error-rate (5xx + prompt failures) > 0.9% for a 10-minute sliding window OR p95 latency > 450ms for 10 minutes
- Audit: full request/response logs retained per customer retention policy, and telemetry exported to the shared Rollouts dashboard

Attachments: tressel_mvp_map.pdf (customer-facing plan), canary_telemetry_gates.xlsx (gating thresholds + queries)

Request: need operational sign-off from Reliability (Rishi) and engineering/SE sign-off on the gating queries (Karthik/Marissa) so I can send the formal exception language to Procurement/legal. Can we get a decision today? Tressel wants the pilot to start next week.

Thanks —

Naomi —

Thanks for the write-up. I like the conservative approach. A few engineering notes / tweaks to make gating practical:

- Error definition: combine 5xx, runtime prompt-exceptions, and >20% malformed structured outputs as "failure" for gating queries. This avoids noisy client-side failures that look like errors.
- Telemetry windows: use two windows — a short 10-min window for immediate autorevert + a 60-min window for sustained rollback decisions (prevents flapping).
- Health metric: add "KV cache miss rate" as a secondary metric — high miss rate correlates with latency cliffs for long-context customers. Threshold: >18% over 10 minutes should be considered an escalation (not immediate autorevert).
- Rollback action: automatic immediate traffic shift to v1 (zero dwell) and create an incident with the "Rollout-AutoRevert" tag.

If we follow this, I can provide the exact PromQL/SQL queries and the dashboard panels by EOD.

-Karthik
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Adding operational checklist and ask for Legal/Procurement language.

Key operational items to include in the exception packet we send to Procurement:
- Explicit canary duration: 48 hours of pinned version for rollback investigation window; after 48 hours, auto-unpin unless a formal change request is opened.
- Manual override: CS/SEs can force-pin for up to 72 hours but must file a post-mortem if any autorevert triggers occurred.
- Visibility: the customer-facing status page must include an explicit fallback note during the canary window.
- SLA carve: include a clause that our availability SLO for the POC is contingent on the approved rollout policy and telemetry gates.

I've drafted suggested wording for Procurement (see paragraph below) — can one of you confirm this is acceptable from a reliability standpoint? If Rishi signs off, Naomi I can attach this to the deal record and ask Procurement to accept the carveout.

Draft sentence for contract: "Customer acknowledges that during the initial pilot deployment, Redwood Inference will use a staged canary and automated fallback policy; availability commitments are conditioned on the agreed telemetry gates and automatic fallback behaviors documented in Appendix A."

Approved with conditions —

I approve the proposed canary + pin approach for the Tressel POC provided we implement the following mandatory controls before we flip any traffic:

1) Gate implementation: Karthik to provide the concrete queries and confirm the Rollouts dashboard panels are in place (10-min & 60-min windows).
2) Auto-revert thresholds: immediate autorevert if failure-rate > 0.9% over 10 minutes OR p95 latency > 450ms over 10 minutes.
3) Escalation window: if autorevert triggers, do not reintroduce new canary traffic for at least 2 hours; incident post-mortem required within 48 hours.
4) Pin policy: permitted pin up to 48 hours by default; Sales may request extension to 72 hours but must get an explicit sign-off from Reliability + Eng Manager.
5) Logging & audits: enable request-level traces for the canary cohort and snapshot the KV cache metrics at 1-minute granularity for the duration of the pilot.

Assuming the above are in place, Naomi — proceed to submit the exception packet to Procurement with Marissa's draft wording. Rishi (signed)

- Rishi Malhotra
